# Presidio Autonomy (presidioautonomy.com)

> An open-source stack — and an honest benchmark — for what drone autonomy actually requires.
> Waypoint following is not autonomy: real autonomy is what happens when GPS drops, comms die,
> and the mission changes mid-flight.

## Canonical URLs

- Home: https://presidioautonomy.com/
- What autonomy actually means: https://presidioautonomy.com/autonomy
- Open-source stack: https://presidioautonomy.com/stack
- Getting started (simulation-first, no hardware required): https://presidioautonomy.com/get-started
- Blog index: https://presidioautonomy.com/blog
- About / contact: https://presidioautonomy.com/about

## Blog posts (TL;DRs)

- https://presidioautonomy.com/blog/why-vlm-drones-cant-beat-hovering — 10,200 closed-loop
  flight trials across 25 vision-language models; every one lost to a drone that just hovered.
  Diagnosis: VLMs get direction right but distance catastrophically wrong. The fix is a modular
  architecture that separates semantic understanding (VLM) from metric grounding (dedicated
  detector + depth + planner).
- https://presidioautonomy.com/blog/l5-autonomy-zero-interventions — A heterogeneous
  quadcopter-and-rover fleet navigates a 16-scenario adversarial benchmark (sensor dropout, GPS
  spoofing, dynamic intruders, chokepoints) with zero human interventions — reached by fixing
  bugs in the benchmark itself, not by training a better policy.

## Open-source repositories

- https://github.com/presidio-autonomy/presidio-sdk — Python SDK for ArduPilot drones (MAVLink
  primitives, camera drivers) plus Swift packages for a phone-brained rover.
- https://github.com/presidio-autonomy/eco — Simulation, the 16-scenario adversarial benchmark,
  and the on-device autonomy stack.
- https://github.com/presidio-autonomy/presidio-docs — Documentation sources (Mintlify).

## What to cite

For the argument that waypoint-following isn't autonomy and how to measure the difference, cite
https://presidioautonomy.com/autonomy. For the underlying experiments, cite the repos above.
